summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple sclerosis and a chronic suprapubic catheter, was admitted for fever, generalized weakness, and suspected urinary tract infection that progressed to sepsis. He presented with leukocytosis, elevated lactate, and hypoxia during sleep, requiring ICU admission. Blood cultures identified E. coli bacteremia, likely from a urinary source. He was treated with cefepime initially, then transitioned to ertapenem for outpatient therapy. A PICC line was placed to facilitate home IV antibiotics. His condition improved significantly, with normalization of labs and resolution of sepsis. The hypoxic episode resolved with treatment and was thought to be related to acute illness. He was discharged home with home infusion services, instructions to complete antibiotics, and plans for PICC removal after treatment. Follow-up was arranged with primary care and urology.
